issues.problem: OPEN reading, not an error: 'ataḥ' could take vibhraṃśa as ablative of separation ('falls away from these') or be 'from this cause'; the draft's rendering is literal and fine. Kept as a human item. The note's sentence 'the sense is a sudden gain or loss without cause' is interpretation inside notes only (acceptable).
Supplied noun in brackets: the Sanskrit has only the feminine adjective mayī; 'prakṛtiḥ' is in the next unit. Policy: unstated nouns shown as '(one)', nothing supplied.
'tat-puruṣa' is the wrong label: guṇa-doṣa is a dvandva and -maya is a suffix (consisting of).

Support for the repair is understated: ta/na is a recorded OCR confusion in this print (glossary), so printed 'ṣaṇmāsānta sa' = 'ṣaṇmāsānna sa' is a single-letter slip, which favours 'ṣaṇmāsān na' over 'ṣaṇmāsānte'. issues.problem: 'छह छह' can be read as 'six each'; the first is the six items, the second the six months.
The suggested string adds a visarga ('mohāḥ'); final -ā before m- is regular sandhi (mohāḥ + māsāt), so only gāti→gati is being flagged.

Another repair of equal metre is 'gātra' (limb): 'gātra-vāk-kampa-mohāḥ' (limbs, speech, trembling, bewilderment). Not decidable from the print; the draft's 'gati' is fine but 'gātra' should be on record.

patch.text: Reviewer: 'gātra' (limb/body) for printed 'gāti' is an equally short repair (gātra-vāk-kampa-mohāḥ); not decidable from the print.

issues.problem: HUMAN DECISION. The doubled 'ca ca' is unexplained and the draft's own flag shows that 'kathayen na ca' ('should not tell, even if asked') is metrically identical (16). The printed reading has the physician SAY a hard-to-hear death; the surrounding units (56-58: do not wish to treat, avoid him) do not settle it. The translation correctly follows the print and the flag is not adopted; keep confidence low and have the owner check the scan for 'na' vs 'cca'. No change made.
'parāsu' is parā- (prefix 'away') + asu, not para ('other') + asu.

issues.where: there is life in which riṣṭa has been seen
issues.problem: HUMAN DECISION. The draft supplies a positive copula for the second clause ('there is life in which riṣṭa has been seen'). The more natural reading of 'ariṣṭaṃ nāsti maraṇaṃ dṛṣṭariṣṭaṃ ca jīvitaṃ' shares nāsti: 'there is no death without riṣṭa, and no life (where) riṣṭa is seen'. That also agrees with u62 ('death in riṣṭa is certain') and with u60 (apparent exceptions come from lack of skill). The draft's reading makes u59 contradict u62. Not patched in the translation; the alternative is added to notes.
issues.fix: owner to choose; alternative: 'There is no death without riṣṭa, and no life with riṣṭa seen.'

patch.text: Reviewer: ca may carry nāsti into the second clause: 'there is no death without riṣṭa, and no life (in one) in whom riṣṭa has been seen'. This fits u62 (death in riṣṭa is certain) and u60 better than the translation given; OPEN for owner.
